name: Syndromic Congenital Sodium Diarrhea
aliases: Congenital Sodium Diarrhea with Syndromic Features

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Syndromic Congenital Sodium Diarrhea

criteria.description: Persistent watery diarrhea with high sodium content from birth
Histopathological abnormalities of the intestinal mucosa including villous atrophy
Presence of syndromic features such as facial dysmorphism, growth retardation, or congenital anomalies
Identification of pathogenic variants in associated genes (e.g., SLC9A3 or others)
Exclusion of infectious, allergic, or other congenital diarrheal disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of persistent sodium-rich diarrhea from birth, intestinal mucosal abnormalities on biopsy, and syndromic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and histological criteria are met.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent congenital watery diarrhea with high sodium concentration
Severe hyponatremia due to sodium loss in stool
searchTerms: low salt levels due to stool loss

pathognomonic.symptomName: Facial dysmorphism including broad nasal bridge and hypertelorism
searchTerms: broad nasal area and wide-set eyes

common.symptomName: Failure to thrive and growth retardation
searchTerms: failure to gain weight and grow
growth delay and failure to thrive

common.symptomName: Metabolic alkalosis secondary to electrolyte imbalance
searchTerms: blood too alkaline from electrolyte problems
metabolic alkalosis due to salt imbalance
high blood pH from electrolyte issues

common.symptomName: Congenital anomalies such as choanal atresia or limb malformations
searchTerms: birth defects like blocked nasal passages

occasional.symptomName: Chronic metabolic bone disease due to electrolyte imbalance
searchTerms: bone issues due to mineral imbalance
epileptic episodes due to low sodium

laboratory: Metabolic alkalosis on blood gas analysis
imaging: Abdominal ultrasound may show bowel wall thickening
Skeletal X-rays may reveal metabolic bone disease
other: Intestinal biopsy showing villous atrophy and epithelial abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: High chloride concentration in stool instead of sodium
Severe congenital diarrhea with microvillus inclusions on biopsy

redFlags: Severe dehydration refractory to standard treatment
Failure to thrive with syndromic congenital anomalies
